title: T1589.001 — Gather Victim Identity Information - Credentials
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Gather Victim Identity Information - Credentials with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated simulation: Credential capture with an adversary-in-the-middle kit. It shows each step of the technique and what defenders can see. A written version of every step is in the story below the canvas. Use the step buttons under the canvas, or focus the canvas and press the left and right arrow keys.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: Registers the lookalike domain, sends the lure, and replays the stolen session. Everything happens outside your network until the final sign-in.

nodes.label: Phish kit
nodes.tip: An adversary-in-the-middle kit: a pixel-perfect copy of your login page with a proxy that records every value the victim types.

nodes.label: Mail relay
nodes.tip: The sending infrastructure for the phishing email. Fresh domains each week keep delivery rates high.

nodes.label: Finance staff
nodes.tip: Finance-team members whose names and roles were harvested during identity reconnaissance, the parent technique T1589.

nodes.label: Identity provider
nodes.tip: The identity provider (IdP) checks passwords and MFA and issues session tokens. It sees a normal login, because the kit relays it.

nodes.label: SOC
nodes.tip: Your detection and response team. They correlate user reports, risk alerts, and gateway telemetry.

nodes.label: Intel + risk
nodes.tip: Certificate transparency feeds, leak monitoring, and the identity provider's risk engine. They spot the campaign outside the mailbox.

steps.title: Register the lookalike domain
steps.caption: The attacker registers a typo-squatted domain that imitates the Aurelia Pay sign-in portal and hosts a pixel-perfect fake SSO page on it.
steps.defender: Certificate transparency logs publish the new certificate within hours. A brand-matching feed is the earliest technical signal you can get.

steps.title: Harvest the employee list
steps.caption: Using the parent technique, the attacker collects names, roles, and the email format of the finance team from public profiles and old leak data.
steps.defender: List building happens outside your systems. Review how much of your org chart is public.

steps.title: Send the credential lure
steps.caption: A rented mail relay delivers a security-check email to the finance team. The link points to the fake SSO page, not to your real one.
steps.defender: The mail gateway is your first corporate telemetry. Log senders, links, and verdicts so you can scope later.

steps.title: The victim enters the password
steps.caption: One finance employee clicks the link and types the work password into the fake page. To them, the page behaves exactly like the real one.
steps.defender: Your identity provider sees nothing yet. A user report is the only fast way to catch this step.

steps.title: The kit relays and grabs MFA
steps.caption: The adversary-in-the-middle kit forwards the login to the real identity provider, shows the genuine MFA prompt, and records the code and the new session cookie.
steps.defender: The identity provider logs an ordinary successful login. Only odd browser fingerprints or proxy IP addresses give it away.

steps.title: Sign-in from a new location
steps.caption: The attacker replays the stolen session cookie through their proxy. The identity provider sees a successful sign-in from another country: impossible travel.
steps.defender: The risk engine flags the sign-in. The alert is only useful if someone triages it while the session is still active.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: The SOC connects the dots
steps.caption: A user report of the phishing email lands in the security queue while the risk alert waits in the backlog. Correlating both turns two weak signals into one strong case.
steps.defender: Reports and risk alerts live in different tools. Automated correlation, or a tight triage habit, finds the match.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Respond and block
steps.caption: The SOC revokes all sessions, forces a password reset, removes the attacker's inbox rule, and blocks the lookalike domain at the gateway, proxy, and DNS.
steps.defender: Revoke sessions together with the reset. A reset alone leaves the stolen cookie valid until it expires.
